explanation: Diaries comparing parents who switched to home working with parents who did not show an extra hour with children only in the first group, which supports the claim. Blurred boundaries between work and family, company policies and children's game time do not measure time spent together.

stem:
A seventeenth-century chronicle describes a famine in part of the Deccan and says that the rains failed that year. A historian claims that drought was the main cause of the famine.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the historian's claim?
options: The chronicle also describes serious floods in a different province during the same year as the famine.
Famines in the same region in later centuries were also often linked to the failure of the rains.
Grain prices in the region's markets rose very sharply during the year in which the famine began.
Tree rings from that region show normal growth for that year and the years before it, indicating ordinary rainfall.
explanation: Tree rings record rainfall independently of the chronicle, and normal growth suggests the rains did not fail, which undermines drought as the cause. Floods elsewhere do not concern this region, later famines linked to drought would support the historian, and high grain prices fit any famine.

stem:
A household in Faisalabad replaced all its old bulbs with LED bulbs at the start of April. Comparing April with March, it found that the electricity used for lighting fell by more than half: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: fans used 90 units in March but 140 units in April.
lighting used 60 units in March but only 25 units in April.
total use rose from 220 units in March to 237 units in April.
lighting used 60 units in March and 72 units in April.
explanation: Lighting fell from 60 to 25 units, and 25 is less than half of 60. The fan and total figures are accurate but concern other uses, and 72 units is the refrigerator's April figure.

stem:
A researcher claims that shoppers at a Karachi supermarket buy more fruit when it is displayed near the entrance rather than at the back of the store.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim?
options: Shoppers who bought fruit at the supermarket usually also bought bread and milk on the same visit.
Most of the supermarket's fruit is supplied by farms in the interior of Sindh and in southern Punjab.
Fruit sales at the supermarket are highest in the summer months, when mangoes, melons and lychees are all in season.
In weeks when fruit was moved to the entrance, fruit sales rose by a quarter while total sales stayed level.
explanation: Moving the display and seeing fruit sales rise, with overall sales unchanged, links the higher sales to the entrance position. What else fruit buyers purchase, where the fruit comes from and seasonal patterns do not test the effect of the display's location.

stem:
A student claims that her phone's battery runs down quickly because of one particular game she plays.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the student's claim?
options: The game uses bright, fast-moving graphics and plays music for as long as it is open.
Her phone is three years old and was bought from a shop in Lahore's Hafeez Centre.
On days when she did not play the game at all, her battery ran down just as quickly.
Several of her friends also play the same game on their own phones every day.
explanation: If the battery drains just as fast without the game, the game is not the cause. Bright graphics and music would support her claim, and the phone's age or her friends' habits do not test it.

stem:
A city museum asked 400 visitors which of its four galleries they liked most. The curator noted that more than a third of the visitors surveyed chose the miniature paintings gallery: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 140 of the 400 visitors named it as their favourite.
120 of the 400 visitors named it as their favourite.
140 of the 400 visitors named the sculpture gallery.
60 of the 400 visitors named it, fewer than textiles.
explanation: The miniature paintings gallery was chosen by 140 visitors, which is 35 percent of 400 and so more than a third. The figure 120 belongs to sculpture (30 percent), and 60 is the coins gallery's figure.

stem:
Algae blooms appear each year in a lake near a small town in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. A researcher claims that the blooms are caused by fertiliser washing off nearby farms rather than by sewage from the town.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim?
options: Water samples from the lake contain high levels of the nutrients that encourage algae to grow quickly.
The town's population has roughly doubled since the first algae blooms were noticed on the lake.
Blooms appear mainly in the weeks after farmers spread fertiliser, even in years when the town's sewage was diverted away from the lake.
Algae blooms make the lake's water unsafe for swimming for several weeks in each summer season.
explanation: Blooms that follow fertiliser spreading and continue when sewage is diverted point to farm runoff and away from sewage. High nutrient levels fit either source, and a growing town would favour the sewage explanation.

stem:
A student measured the height of a bean seedling at the end of each week. The plant grew more each week than in the week before: between the ends of weeks 3 and 4, it grew ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 6 cm, more than the 5 cm it grew between weeks 2 and 3.
5 cm, more than the 4 cm it grew between weeks 1 and 2.
18 cm, more than the 12 cm it grew between weeks 2 and 3.
6 cm, less than the 7 cm it grew between weeks 2 and 3.
explanation: From week 3 to week 4 the plant went from 12 cm to 18 cm, a gain of 6 cm, and from week 2 to week 3 it gained 5 cm (7 to 12). The choice with 18 and 12 confuses heights with growth, and 5 cm is the growth between weeks 2 and 3, not weeks 3 and 4.

stem:
An environmental scientist measured average air-quality index (AQI) readings at four stations in a city during November; higher readings mean more polluted air. She claims that pollution is worst next to the city's industrial zone and eases steadily with distance from it. ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the scientist's claim?
options: Readings fell at each step, from 210 at the station 1 km from the zone to 120 at the station 12 km away.
The station 4 km from the zone averaged 175, lower than the 210 recorded at the station only 1 km away.
All four stations recorded averages above 100, including the station that was farthest from the zone.
Readings rose at each step, from 120 at the station nearest the zone to 210 at the station farthest from it.
explanation: The readings drop at every station as distance grows (210, 175, 140, 120), which shows pollution worst near the zone and easing steadily. The comparison of just two stations shows only part of the pattern, every station being above 100 says nothing about distance, and the last choice reverses the table.

stem:
Staff at an animal shelter in Karachi claim that the shelter's cats are calmer when classical music is played.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the staff's claim?
options: The shelter plays its music through speakers placed close to where the cats usually sleep.
Staff at the shelter said that they enjoyed their work more on days when music was playing.
On days with classical music, the cats showed fewer signs of stress, such as hiding and pacing.
Most of the cats at the shelter were adopted by new owners within two months of first arriving there.
explanation: Fewer stress behaviours on music days is direct evidence that the cats are calmer, as the staff claim. The position of the speakers, the staff's own enjoyment and adoption rates do not measure the cats' behaviour.

stem:
In Sameena Durrani's novel The Night Train, Imran avoids arguments with his father and rarely speaks up at work. A student argues that Imran is simply a coward. A later scene in the novel, however, suggests otherwise: ______

Which quotation from The Night Train most effectively challenges the student's claim?
options: "When fire spread to the rear carriage, it was Imran who went back through the smoke to carry out the guard."
"Imran said nothing when his father sold the shop, though he had worked in it every day since he was twelve."
"Imran liked to sit by the window and count the small stations as they slid past in the darkness outside."
"Imran's manager often forgot his name and called him by his elder brother's name instead of his own."
explanation: Going back into a burning carriage to rescue someone is an act of courage, which directly challenges the view that Imran is a coward. His silence about the shop supports the student, and counting stations or being misnamed shows nothing about bravery.

stem:
A linguist claims that speakers of a dialect in a remote mountain valley have kept an old form of the word for "water" that has disappeared from the lowland dialects.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the linguist's claim?
options: Speakers of the mountain dialect also use many words that they have borrowed from neighbouring languages.
The mountain dialect is spoken today by about 30,000 people living in a small number of valleys.
Lowland speakers sometimes say they find the mountain dialect hard to follow in ordinary conversation.
The same form appears in centuries-old lowland manuscripts but is no longer used by any lowland speakers.
explanation: Finding the mountain form in old lowland texts, but not in lowland speech today, shows that it is an older form the lowlands have lost. Borrowed words, the number of speakers and how hard the dialect is to follow say nothing about this word's history.

stem:
A university reported applications and admissions for its three faculties. An education writer argues that Engineering was the most selective faculty, admitting the smallest share of its applicants, even though it admitted the largest number of students. ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the writer's argument?
options: Engineering admitted 400 students, more than either Business, which admitted 300, or Arts, which admitted only 240 students.
Engineering received 2,000 applications, which was more than the number that Arts and Business received combined.
Engineering admitted 400 of 2,000 applicants, or 20 percent, more students than the others but a smaller share than Business (25 percent) or Arts (30 percent).
Arts admitted 240 of its 800 applicants, or 30 percent, which was the largest share admitted by any of the three faculties.
explanation: Engineering admitted 20 percent (400 ÷ 2,000), below Business's 25 percent (300 ÷ 1,200) and Arts's 30 percent (240 ÷ 800), while admitting the most students, so this choice supports both parts. The choice about 400 students shows only the number, Arts and Business together received exactly 2,000 applications, not fewer, and the Arts figure does not mention Engineering.

stem:
A shopkeeper in Sialkot claims that his umbrellas sell well only when it is raining.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the shopkeeper's claim?
options: His umbrella sales rose sharply during the first week of the monsoon rains in July.
His shop also sells raincoats, rubber boots and plastic covers for motorcycle seats and handlebars.
Most of the umbrellas he sells are made in a small factory in nearby Gujranwala.
During a dry, sunny week in June, he sold just as many umbrellas to people wanting shade.
explanation: Strong sales in dry, sunny weather contradict the claim that umbrellas sell well only in rain. A rise during the monsoon fits the claim, and his other stock or the umbrellas' origin is irrelevant.

stem:
Many people believe that a nineteenth-century school in Peshawar taught only boys. A historian argues that it admitted girls as well.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historian's claim?
options: The school building had two separate entrances, one on each side of its courtyard.
Several new schools for girls opened elsewhere in the region in the early 1900s.
The school's surviving register for 1885 lists the names of 14 girls among its pupils.
The school taught arithmetic, Persian, Urdu and English to all of the pupils who attended it.
explanation: A register naming girls as pupils is direct evidence that the school admitted them. Two entrances could have many explanations, schools opened elsewhere later say nothing about this one, and the subjects taught do not show who was enrolled.

stem:
A bookshop in Lahore sells books in Urdu and in English. In 2020 it sold more English books than Urdu books, but this changed over the next three years. According to the table, Urdu books first outsold English books in ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 2022, when the shop sold 3,900 Urdu books and 3,800 English books.
2023, when the shop sold 4,300 Urdu books and 3,600 English books.
2021, when the shop sold 3,600 Urdu books and 3,900 English books.
2020, when the shop sold 4,100 Urdu books and 3,200 English books.
explanation: 2022 is the first year in which Urdu sales (3,900) were higher than English sales (3,800). Urdu books also led in 2023, but that was not the first time, in 2021 English books still led, and the 2020 choice swaps the two figures.

stem:
A technology reviewer claims that a new phone's camera takes better photos in low light than a rival phone's camera does. Her evidence is a set of photos she took with both phones in the streets of the old city at night.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the reviewer's claim?
options: The new phone's camera has a larger image sensor than the camera in the rival phone has.
The new phone costs about Rs 20,000 more in the shops than the rival phone does.
She took her photos with the rival phone's night mode switched off but the new phone's night mode switched on.
Her night photos were later shared widely on social media by thousands of the readers who follow her reviews.
explanation: If only one phone had its night mode on, the test was unfair, so the photos cannot show that its camera is better. A larger sensor would make the claim more likely, and price or social media sharing says nothing about photo quality.

stem:
People in a mountain community in Gilgit-Baltistan cope unusually well with the thin air at high altitude. A geneticist claims that this ability is mainly inherited rather than developed through a lifetime of living at altitude.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the geneticist's claim?
options: Children of the community raised near sea level showed the same ability on their first visit to high altitude.
Members of the community who have lived longest at high altitude show the ability most strongly of all.
Visitors from the plains often suffer headaches during their first few days in the community's villages.
The ability lets the body make more efficient use of the oxygen in the air when the air is thin.
explanation: Children who never lived at altitude but still have the ability cannot have developed it by living there, which points to inheritance. Stronger ability among long-term residents would suggest it is developed, and the visitors' headaches or how the ability works does not decide between the two.

stem:
A tea stall in Rawalpindi recorded how many cups of tea it sold on four days. Sales were highest on Wednesday, at ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 260 cups, 20 more than on Monday.
240 cups, 10 more than on Thursday.
260 cups, 30 more than on Monday.
230 cups, 25 more than on Tuesday.
explanation: Wednesday's 260 cups are 20 more than Monday's 240. The 30-cup gap is a subtraction slip, and the choices giving 240 and 230 cups describe Monday and Thursday.

stem:
A museum curator claims that a carpet in the museum's collection was woven in Central Asia rather than in Lahore, where the museum bought it.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the curator's claim?
options: Its pattern of repeated red medallions appears in carpets woven in many regions of Asia.
Tests show that its wool comes from a breed of sheep that, at that time, was raised only in Central Asia.
The museum bought the carpet from a dealer in the old city of Lahore in the early 1950s.
It has about 120 knots per square centimetre, which makes it an unusually fine and tightly woven carpet for its period.
explanation: Wool from a sheep found only in Central Asia ties the carpet's making to that region. A pattern used in many regions cannot place it, the purchase in Lahore says where it was sold, not woven, and fineness alone does not point to a place.

stem:
In a survey of 300 shoppers at a market in Hyderabad, 180 said they would bring cloth bags instead of buying plastic ones if plastic bags cost Rs 10 each, while 90 said they would do so if plastic bags cost Rs 5 each. A city official claims that a higher charge would persuade more shoppers to switch to cloth bags.

Which choice most effectively uses the survey results to support the official's claim?
options: More than half of the 300 shoppers said that they would switch at a charge of only Rs 5.
Twice as many shoppers said they would switch at a charge of Rs 10 as at a charge of Rs 5.
Of the 300 shoppers surveyed, 180 said that they already bring cloth bags to the market.
Only 90 of the shoppers said that they would switch at either of the two levels of charge.
explanation: 180 shoppers at Rs 10 against 90 at Rs 5 is double, so the higher charge persuades more people, as the official claims. 90 is less than half of 300, the 180 were answering about a Rs 10 charge rather than current habits, and 180 shoppers, not 90, would switch at Rs 10.

stem:
A swimming coach in Lahore claims that her swimmers improve faster when they train in the morning than when they train in the evening.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the coach's claim?
options: The pool is much less crowded early in the morning than it is in the evening after school.
Swimmers who moved to morning training cut their times more over a term than those who kept training in the evening.
Most of the swimmers said in a survey that they much preferred training in the evening to training early in the morning.
The swimmers train for 90 minutes a session, five days a week, throughout the school term.
explanation: Comparing how much morning and evening trainers improved tests the claim directly, and the morning group improved more. A quieter pool might explain a benefit but does not show one, and the swimmers' preferences or training hours do not compare improvement.

stem:
Between 2018 and 2022, smartphone prices in a country fell sharply and the use of mobile banking rose sharply. An economist claims that cheaper smartphones caused the rise in mobile banking by putting phones in the hands of new users.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the economist's claim?
options: Smartphone prices in the country fell by about a third in total between 2018 and 2022.
Banks in the country also opened a large number of new branches in rural areas between 2018 and 2022.
Mobile banking was more widely used in the country's cities than in its villages.
Mobile banking grew just as fast among people who owned smartphones before 2018 as among new owners.
explanation: If people who already had smartphones took up mobile banking just as quickly, the growth was not mainly driven by new, cheaper phones. The size of the price fall fits the economist's story, and new bank branches or a gap between cities and villages do not test it.

stem:
In Nadia Hussain's novel The Glassblower's Son, the narrator, Faraz, deeply admires his father's skill but fears that he himself will never match it: ______

Which quotation from The Glassblower's Son most effectively illustrates the claim?
options: "My father's vases were famous across Hyderabad, and buyers came from as far away as Karachi just to watch him at work in the shop."
"I knew from my very first day in the workshop that before long I would be blowing glass far better than my father ever had."
"I could watch my father turn a glowing lump into a perfect vase all day, and each time I was sure my own hands would never learn the trick."
"The furnace roared from dawn until dusk, and in the summer months the heat in the workshop was almost too much to bear."
explanation: The quotation shows both admiration (watching his father all day) and fear of never equalling him (his hands would never learn), which are the two parts of the claim. The quotation about famous vases shows the father's reputation but not Faraz's fear, and the one about soon surpassing his father contradicts it.

stem:
At a college in Lahore, Biology was the most popular optional subject among first-year students, chosen by ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 88 students, 8 more than chose Economics.
96 students, more than chose Economics and Psychology together.
72 students, 8 more than chose Psychology.
96 students, 8 more than chose Computer Science.
explanation: Biology was chosen by 96 students, 8 more than Computer Science's 88. Economics and Psychology together had 136 students, and the choices with 88 and 72 give other subjects' figures.

stem:
A biologist claims that a songbird species begins its autumn migration in response to shortening days rather than falling temperatures.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the biologist's claim?
options: In the wild, the birds begin migrating in late September, when the days are shortening quickly.
The birds fly mainly at night on their long journey south and then rest and feed in fields during the daytime.
Birds kept indoors under long artificial days still became restless to migrate when their room was cooled.
Birds kept indoors under short artificial days became restless to migrate even in a warm room.
explanation: If cooling alone triggers migration restlessness while the days stay long, temperature rather than day length is at work, which weakens the claim. Restlessness under short days in a warm room would support the biologist, and the timing in the wild fits both explanations.

stem:
An agricultural officer surveyed 250 farmers in a Punjab district about whether they check weather forecasts on their phones. He reports that younger farmers were far more likely to do so than older farmers. ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the officer's report?
options: More farmers aged 35–55 were surveyed than farmers in either of the other two age groups in the district.
Of the 80 farmers under 35, 64 (80 percent) checked forecasts, against 12 of the 60 over 55 (20 percent).
Of the 250 farmers surveyed in the district, 131 said that they checked weather forecasts on their phones.
Of the 110 farmers aged 35–55, 55 (50 percent) checked forecasts, a higher share than in any other group.
explanation: Comparing shares in the youngest and oldest groups, 64 ÷ 80 = 80 percent against 12 ÷ 60 = 20 percent, shows the gap the officer reports. The sample sizes and the overall total of 131 are accurate but say nothing about age, and 50 percent is lower than the under-35 group's 80 percent.

stem:
A student in Multan claims that the power cuts in her neighbourhood happen only in the evening.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the student's claim?
options: Power cuts in her neighbourhood often begin at around seven o'clock in the evening.
Her family bought a small generator last year so that the fans and lights can keep running during power cuts.
Her family's log shows a two-hour power cut that began at ten o'clock on a Tuesday morning.
Power cuts in her city happen more often during the summer than during the winter.
explanation: A morning power cut is a clear exception to a claim that cuts happen only in the evening. Cuts that begin at seven in the evening fit the claim, and the generator or seasonal pattern does not address the time of day.

stem:
A marketing researcher claims that people trust an online product review more when the review mentions a small flaw in the product.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim?
options: Readers rated positive reviews that mentioned one minor flaw as more trustworthy than reviews full of praise.
Reviews that mention flaws in a product are, on average, slightly longer than reviews that do not.
Most online shoppers say that they read at least three reviews before deciding to buy a product.
Products with a large number of reviews tend to sell better online than similar products that have only a few reviews.
explanation: Readers judging reviews with a small flaw as more trustworthy is exactly what the claim predicts. The length of reviews, how many reviews shoppers read and the link between review numbers and sales do not measure trust in a review that mentions a flaw.

stem:
An education officer notes that the gap between boys' and girls' school enrolment did not narrow in every district between 2015 and 2023. In Zhob, for instance, ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: girls' enrolment rose from 40 to 44 percent, but boys' enrolment rose faster, from 62 to 70 percent.
girls' enrolment rose from 40 to 44 percent, while boys' enrolment rose by the same amount, from 62 to 66 percent.
girls' enrolment rose from 40 to 44 percent, which was a smaller rise than girls' enrolment showed in Swat or Chitral.
the gap fell from 22 points to 10 points, because girls' enrolment rose faster than boys' enrolment did.
explanation: In Zhob the gap grew from 22 points (62 − 40) to 26 points (70 − 44), because boys' enrolment rose by 8 points and girls' by only 4, which illustrates the officer's point. Boys' enrolment in Zhob reached 70, not 66, the comparison with other districts' girls says nothing about the gap, and the fall from 22 to 10 points describes Swat.

stem:
A literary scholar argues that a twentieth-century Urdu poet's early poems were strongly influenced by the Persian poetry she studied as a girl.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the scholar's claim?
options: Her later poems were written mostly in free verse rather than in the traditional forms she first used.
She was born in Lahore and studied at a girls' school there before going on to university in the city.
Her poems first appeared in print in a literary magazine in 1962, when she was twenty-three years old.
Her childhood notebooks hold copies of Persian ghazals, and her early poems borrow images from them line for line.
explanation: Notebooks of Persian ghazals from her childhood, with images taken from them in her early poems, tie those poems directly to Persian influence. Her later style, her schooling and the date of her first publication do not show what influenced her early work.

stem:
Sales of home air purifiers in Lahore doubled in November 2023. A business journalist claims that the rise was driven by growing fears about the city's winter smog.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the journalist's claim?
options: Internet searches for information about smog reached their highest level in Lahore that November.
Air purifiers contain filters that need to be replaced every few months if they are to keep working properly.
Most of the purifiers sold that month were bought by families who had very young children at home.
Throughout November, the best-selling brand of purifier was sold at half price in a nationwide sale.
explanation: A half-price sale on the leading brand offers another explanation for the jump in sales, so the rise cannot confidently be put down to smog fears. A peak in smog searches supports the journalist, families with young children buying purifiers fits fear of smog, and filter replacement is irrelevant.

stem:
Visitors to a school science fair in Quetta were counted each hour. The busiest hour was ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 10 to 11 am, when 110 visitors came.
12 to 1 pm, when 80 visitors came.
11 am to 12 pm, when 110 visitors came.
9 to 10 am, when just 45 visitors arrived.
explanation: The largest count, 110 visitors, was recorded between 11 am and 12 pm. The choices for 10 to 11 am and 12 to 1 pm attach figures to the wrong hours, and 9 to 10 am was the quietest hour.

stem:
A distant star recently grew much dimmer for several months. An astronomer claims that a cloud of dust passing in front of the star caused the dimming, rather than a drop in the star's own brightness.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the astronomer's claim?
options: The star dimmed more in blue light than in red light, which is what happens when starlight passes through dust.
The star's brightness returned to its usual level after about six months and has stayed steady since then.
Stars of this type sometimes dim on their own as they near the end of their lives and begin to cool.
The star lies about 500 light-years from Earth, in a part of the sky that is easy to observe in winter.
explanation: Greater dimming in blue light than in red is the known sign of dust in the way, so it supports the astronomer. Recovery after six months fits either cause, stars dimming on their own points to the rival explanation, and the star's distance is irrelevant.

stem:
A researcher found that neighbourhoods in a city with more cafés tend to have higher rents. She claims that the opening of new cafés drives rents up.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researcher's claim?
options: Cafés in high-rent neighbourhoods usually charge more for a cup of coffee than cafés in other parts of the city.
Several of the city's most popular cafés have recently opened second branches in nearby towns.
In most of the neighbourhoods, rents had begun to climb several years before any new cafés opened.
Most cafés in the city stay open from early in the morning until quite late at night.
explanation: If rents were rising before the cafés arrived, the cafés cannot have started the rise, and rising rents may instead have attracted them. Higher coffee prices in pricey areas, new branches elsewhere and opening hours do not address which came first.

stem:
A book club in Islamabad tracks members' ratings of the books it reads. One member points out that the book with the highest average rating was also among the least rated: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: The Last Caravan received 140 ratings, the most of any book, but it had the lowest average rating of 3.9.
Glass Rivers had an average rating of 4.4 from 60 ratings, which was the second-highest average of the four.
Winter in Swat had the highest average rating, 4.2, and it received 85 ratings, the second-largest number.
The Salt Road had the highest average, 4.6, but only 12 ratings, far fewer than any other book.
explanation: The Salt Road's 4.6 is the top average, and its 12 ratings are the fewest, which is exactly the member's point. The Last Caravan and Glass Rivers choices are accurate but do not concern the top-rated book, and Winter in Swat's 4.2 is not the highest average.

stem:
A historian claims that a seventeenth-century garden in Lahore was designed above all to be viewed from the raised terrace along one of its sides.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historian's claim?
options: The garden was watered by channels fed from a canal that ran several kilometres away from it.
Visitors today usually enter the garden through a large gate in the middle of its southern wall.
The garden contains more than a dozen kinds of fruit tree, including mango, orange and pomegranate.
Its flower beds were laid out in patterns that form a clear design only when they are seen from above.
explanation: Patterns that make sense only from above suggest that the garden was planned to be seen from a height, such as the terrace. The water supply, today's entrance and the fruit trees say nothing about how the garden was meant to be viewed.

stem:
A student recorded the number of rainy days in four months at her school in Murree. July had the most rainy days, with ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 19 rainy days, 2 more than August.
17 rainy days, 6 more than June.
19 rainy days, 3 more than August.
11 rainy days, 5 more than May.
explanation: July had 19 rainy days and August had 17, a difference of 2. The 3-day gap is a subtraction slip, and the choices with 17 and 11 days describe August and June.

stem:
A pupil claims that the new drinking-water fountains at her school have led pupils to buy fewer bottled drinks.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the pupil's claim?
options: The fountains were installed in the corridors just outside the school's science laboratories.
Pupils said that the water from the fountains tasted cleaner than the tap water in their homes.
The school is planning to install two more fountains beside the sports ground later in the year.
The canteen sold 40 percent fewer bottled drinks in the term after the fountains were put in.
explanation: A sharp fall in canteen sales of bottled drinks after the fountains arrived is exactly what the claim predicts. Where the fountains are, how the water tastes and future plans do not show any change in what pupils buy.

stem:
A year after a large park opened in a district of Faisalabad, reported crime in the streets around it had fallen by 15 percent. A city official claims that the park caused the fall.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the official's claim?
options: Residents who live near the park say that the streets around it now feel much safer to walk along at night.
The park has bright floodlights along all of its main paths and is patrolled by two security guards every evening.
Reported crime fell by about 15 percent across the whole city in that year, including in areas far from the park.
The city plans to open two more parks of a similar size in other districts over the next five years.
explanation: If crime fell just as much everywhere, a citywide cause is more likely than the park, so the official's claim is weakened. Residents feeling safer and the park's lights and guards fit the claim, and plans for new parks are irrelevant.

stem:
In Saira Lakhani's novel A House in Hyderabad, the narrator describes her father as a man of few words but deep feeling: ______

Which quotation from A House in Hyderabad most effectively illustrates the claim?
options: "Abba said nothing when I left for university, but my mother told me that he stood at the gate until the bus was out of sight."
"Abba could talk for hours about cricket, politics and the price of onions, and nobody at the table was ever able to stop him."
"Abba worked at the main post office for thirty years and, as he liked to remind us, he never once arrived there late."
"Abba's house had a blue door that he repainted every spring, a few days before the start of Ramzan."
explanation: Saying nothing at the farewell yet standing at the gate until the bus vanished shows both few words and deep feeling. The quotation about talking for hours shows the opposite, and his punctuality or the blue door shows neither trait.

stem:
A cricketer from Sialkot began working with a new batting coach at the start of the 2021 season. Her batting average rose in every season after 2020, from ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 42 runs per innings in 2020 to 24 in 2023.
31 runs per innings in 2020 to 36 in 2023.
24 runs per innings in 2020 to 42 in 2023.
24 runs per innings in 2020 to 36 in 2021.
explanation: The table shows an average of 24 in 2020 rising each season to 42 in 2023. The other choices reverse the trend or attach averages to the wrong seasons, for example 36 belongs to 2022.

stem:
A researcher studying a desert ant in the Thar claims that, after foraging, the ant finds its way back to its nest mainly by counting its steps.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim?
options: The ants forage alone during the hottest part of the day, when very few of their predators are active on the sand.
The entrance to each nest is surrounded by a small mound of sand that the ants pile up as they dig.
Ants whose legs were lengthened with tiny stilts walked past their nest, while ants with shortened legs stopped short of it.
Ants returning to the nest walk back in a fairly straight line rather than retracing their outward path.
explanation: If longer steps carry ants too far and shorter steps leave them short, they must be judging distance by the number of steps, which supports the claim. A straight return path shows that ants know the direction home but not how they measure distance, and foraging habits or nest mounds are irrelevant.

stem:
A dairy farmer near Okara claims that his cows give more milk when he plays music in the cattle shed.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the farmer's claim?
options: The farmer plays mostly folk songs on a small radio that hangs near the door of the shed.
The cows are milked twice a day, once early in the morning and once in the late afternoon.
In weeks when the music was switched off, the cows gave just as much milk as usual.
Several other farmers in the area have started playing music to their cattle as well.
explanation: If milk output stays the same without music, the music is not raising it. The type of music, milking times and other farmers' habits do not show any effect on milk.

stem:
A traveller compared three ways of making the same journey between two cities in Pakistan. She claims that the train is slower than the bus but cheaper. ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the traveller's claim?
options: The train takes 6.5 hours and costs Rs 1,800, while the bus takes 5.0 hours and costs Rs 2,400.
The flight takes only 1.0 hour but costs Rs 12,000, which is far more than either the train or the bus costs.
The bus takes 5.0 hours, which is 1.5 hours less than the train takes to complete the same journey.
The train takes 5.0 hours and costs Rs 2,400, while the bus takes 6.5 hours and costs Rs 1,800.
explanation: The claim compares the train and the bus on both time and cost, and only the first choice gives both: the train is slower (6.5 against 5.0 hours) and cheaper (Rs 1,800 against Rs 2,400). The flight is irrelevant, the time-only choice leaves out cost, and the last choice swaps the figures.

stem:
A historian argues that a nineteenth-century Karachi merchant learned English mainly from the business letters he received, rather than through formal schooling.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the historian's claim?
options: He later sent all four of his sons to English-medium schools in Karachi and then on to college in Bombay to study law and commerce.
He traded mainly in cotton, wool and hides with firms in Liverpool, Glasgow and London.
His early English letters copy whole phrases from letters sent to him by British firms, including their spelling mistakes.
His English letters grew longer and more frequent as his trading business expanded over the years.
explanation: Copying phrases, and even errors, from letters he received shows him learning English from those letters. His sons' schooling, his trade goods and the growing length of his letters do not show how he himself learned the language.

stem:
A primary-school teacher claims that pupils learn their multiplication tables faster when they learn them through songs.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the teacher's claim?
options: Pupils taught the tables through songs recited them correctly sooner than pupils taught from wall charts.
Pupils said that they enjoyed singing in class more than almost any other activity in the whole of the school day.
The school's music teacher wrote the songs, which use tunes from well-known children's rhymes.
Pupils who already knew their tables well were often asked to lead the rest of the class in singing.
explanation: Comparing how quickly pupils taught by songs and by charts learned the tables tests the claim directly, and the song group was faster. Enjoyment, who wrote the songs and who led the singing do not measure learning speed.

stem:
A fruit seller in Swat claims that although she sold fewer kilos of cherries than of apricots last week, the cherries brought in more money. ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the seller's claim?
options: She sold 50 kg of apricots, which was more than the 30 kg of cherries and the 40 kg of plums that she sold that week.
Cherries cost Rs 600 per kilo, twice the price of apricots and more than twice the price of plums at her stall.
She earned Rs 15,000 from 30 kg of cherries, less than the Rs 18,000 she earned from 50 kg of apricots.
She sold 30 kg of cherries at Rs 600 a kilo, earning Rs 18,000, against Rs 15,000 from 50 kg of apricots at Rs 300.
explanation: Cherries earned 30 × 600 = Rs 18,000 and apricots 50 × 300 = Rs 15,000, so fewer kilos of cherries brought in more money. The choices about kilos alone or prices alone give only half the picture, and the last choice swaps the two totals.

stem:
Students at a Lahore school who take music lessons tend to get higher marks in mathematics than students who do not. A parent claims that the music lessons improve the students' mathematics.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the parent's claim?
options: Music lessons at the school include some practice in counting beats and reading rhythms.
Students who took up music lessons already had higher mathematics marks before their lessons began.
Students who take music lessons say that they enjoy mathematics more than other students do.
The school offers lessons in the harmonium, the tabla and the guitar on three afternoons a week after classes end.
explanation: If the music students were already ahead in mathematics before starting, the lessons cannot explain the gap. Counting beats suggests how music might help, and enjoyment or the instruments offered do not show an effect on marks.

stem:
In Kiran Javed's poem "Night Shift", the speaker, a hospital cleaner, feels that the work she does goes unnoticed by others: ______

Which quotation from "Night Shift" most effectively illustrates the claim?
options: "The ward is quiet after two o'clock, / and the clock ticks louder than the ceiling fans."
"All night I mend what others break, / and in the morning no one asks who swept the floor."
"My colleagues bring me tea and thank me warmly / each morning when I hand the keys to them."
"I walk home as the milk carts pass, / and the city opens its shutters one by one."
explanation: No one asking who swept the floor after a night's work expresses the feeling of being unnoticed. Colleagues thanking her warmly shows the opposite, and the quiet ward and the walk home describe scenes rather than this feeling.

stem:
Four Class 9 sections at a school in Bahawalpur took part in a tree-planting week. Class 9B planted the most trees, ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 46 trees, 5 more than Class 9A.
51 trees, 5 more than Class 9C.
51 trees, 17 more than Class 9C.
34 trees, 5 more than Class 9D.
explanation: Class 9B planted 51 trees and Class 9C planted 46, a difference of 5. The gap of 17 is between 9B and 9A, and the choices with 46 and 34 trees describe other classes.

stem:
A highway engineer claims that a new kind of road surface reduces the noise made by passing traffic.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the engineer's claim?
options: The new surface costs about 15 percent more to lay than the old surface did, though the engineer expects it to last a good deal longer.
Drivers who tried the new surface said that it felt smoother than the old surface at high speeds.
The new surface drains rainwater away more quickly than the old surface, so fewer puddles form.
At equal traffic levels, roadside microphones recorded less noise on stretches with the new surface than on the old one.
explanation: Measuring noise on the two surfaces under the same traffic tests the claim directly, and the new surface was quieter. Cost, drivers' sense of smoothness and drainage do not measure noise.

stem:
Over several decades, the lizards on a small island in the Arabian Sea developed larger heads and stronger jaws. A biologist claims that this happened because the lizards began eating hard-shelled snails.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the biologist's claim?
options: Lizards with larger heads can bite down with greater force than lizards of the same species with smaller heads.
The snails on the island are most plentiful during and just after the summer monsoon rains each year.
The lizards on the island also eat insects, seeds and, from time to time, small pieces of fallen fruit.
Lizards of the same species on a nearby island with no snails developed equally large heads over the same period.
explanation: If lizards without any snails to eat developed equally large heads, the snails cannot explain the change. The link between head size and bite force supports the biologist, and the snails' seasons or the lizards' other foods do not test the claim.

stem:
In 2022, a city library lent 12,000 books, 3,000 of which were e-books. In 2023, it again lent 12,000 books, 4,800 of which were e-books. The librarian claims that e-books made up a larger share of the library's lending in 2023 than in 2022.

Which choice most effectively uses the figures to support the librarian's claim?
options: E-books rose from a quarter of all loans in 2022 to 40 percent of all loans in 2023.
The library lent the same total number of books, 12,000, in each of the two years.
E-books made up more than half of all the books that the library lent out during 2023.
The library lent 1,800 more printed books in 2023 than it had lent in 2022.
explanation: 3,000 of 12,000 is 25 percent and 4,800 of 12,000 is 40 percent, so the e-book share grew. The equal totals alone say nothing about e-books, 40 percent is less than half, and printed loans fell from 9,000 to 7,200 rather than rising.

stem:
A boy in Multan claims that every mango from the old tree in his grandfather's garden is sweet.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the boy's claim?
options: The tree is more than forty years old and very tall.
Two mangoes picked from the tree last week tasted sour.
Mangoes from the tree ripen in late June and July.
His grandfather says the tree's mangoes are the best in Multan.
explanation: Sour mangoes from the same tree contradict the claim that every one is sweet. The tree's age, its ripening season and the grandfather's praise do not count against the claim.

stem:
An urban planner claims that trees along residential streets help keep homes cooler in summer.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the planner's claim?
options: Residents of tree-lined streets said that they valued the birdsong and the shade on their morning walks.
On summer afternoons, homes on tree-lined streets were 3°C cooler indoors than similar homes on nearby bare streets.
Trees along streets take up some of the rainwater that would otherwise flood the roads during storms.
Homes on tree-lined streets usually sell for noticeably higher prices than similar homes on streets that have no trees at all.
explanation: Comparing indoor temperatures in similar homes with and without street trees tests the claim directly, and the tree-lined homes were cooler. Birdsong, rainwater and house prices do not measure temperature.

stem:
An archaeologist claims that a large pit found at an ancient settlement near Mardan was used for storing grain rather than for dumping rubbish.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the archaeologist's claim?
options: The pit was about two metres deep and roughly circular, with steep sides and a flat floor.
Other pits dug at the same settlement were found to be full of animal bones and pieces of broken pottery.
The settlement was lived in for about four hundred years before its people abandoned it.
The pit's walls were lined with clay, and its floor held charred grain but no bones or broken pottery.
explanation: A clay lining suits storage, and grain without bones or broken pots points to grain rather than rubbish. Other pits full of rubbish describe different pits and say nothing about this one, and the pit's shape or how long the site was used does not reveal its purpose.

stem:
A university in Islamabad surveyed students about how they travel to campus, before and after cycle lanes were built nearby. A student journalist reports that the share of surveyed students who cycled to campus tripled: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: 20 of 400 students (5 percent) cycled in 2021, against 75 of 500 (15 percent) in 2023.
75 students cycled to campus in 2023, nearly four times the number of students who cycled there in 2021.
500 students were surveyed in 2023, which was 100 more students than had been surveyed in 2021.
20 of 400 students (20 percent) cycled in 2021, against 75 of 500 (75 percent) in 2023.
explanation: The journalist's point is about the share: 20 ÷ 400 = 5 percent and 75 ÷ 500 = 15 percent, which is three times as large. The count of cyclists ignores the larger sample, the number surveyed says nothing about cycling, and the last choice confuses counts with percentages.

stem:
In Usman Raja's novel Kite Season, the narrator's best friend, Ali, is fiercely competitive: ______

Which quotation from Kite Season most effectively illustrates the claim?
options: "Ali shared his sweets with every child in the lane, even the ones he did not like."
"Ali would rather let the string cut his fingers than let another boy's kite cut his own."
"Ali's kites were always red, like the roof of his grandfather's shop near the canal."
"Ali never minded losing a kite; he would just laugh, shrug and start building a new one at once."
explanation: Preferring injury to losing a kite fight shows a fierce will to win. Not minding defeat shows the opposite, and sharing sweets or the colour of his kites shows nothing about competitiveness.

stem:
An academy in Karachi claims that its exam-preparation course raises students' test scores. As evidence, it notes that students who took the course scored well above the city average.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the academy's claim?
options: The course runs for twelve weeks and includes three full practice tests taken under exam conditions.
Students who chose the course were already scoring well above average on practice tests before it began.
Students who took the course said that it had made them feel much more confident on the day of the exam.
The academy charges Rs 25,000 for the course, which is more than most similar courses in the city.
explanation: If course students were already above average before starting, their high scores cannot be credited to the course. The course's structure, students' confidence and the fee do not show that it raised scores.

stem:
A theatre critic claims that a Pakistani playwright's comedies mock the wealthy rather than the poor.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the critic's claim?
options: In nearly every comedy, the characters made to look foolish are landowners and factory owners, who are outwitted by their servants.
The playwright grew up in a small town in Punjab and later worked for several years as a journalist in Lahore.
The comedies have been performed in many cities across Pakistan and have also been adapted for television.
Several of the comedies are set in grand country houses, with large casts of family members and servants.
explanation: If the foolish characters are almost always the rich, outwitted by the poor, the comedies mock the wealthy, as the critic says. The playwright's background, the plays' popularity and their settings do not show whom they mock.

stem:
A water engineer recorded the level of a small reservoir in Potohar at the start of four months. The level was lowest in ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: April, when it stood at 35 metres.
June, when it stood at 41 metres.
March, when it stood at 38 metres.
May, when it stood at 35 metres.
explanation: The smallest figure in the table is 35 metres, recorded in May. April's level was 38 metres, and the other choices give higher levels or attach figures to the wrong months.

stem:
In a study, students who read short articles on mobile phones understood them less well than students who read the same articles on paper. A researcher concludes that reading on any kind of screen reduces understanding compared with reading on paper.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researcher's claim?
options: Students who read the articles on mobile phones took slightly longer to finish them than students who read them on paper.
Most of the students in the study said that they usually read books for pleasure in printed form.
Students who read the same articles on large tablet screens understood them as well as the paper readers did.
The articles used in the study were all short news reports of about 600 words on everyday topics.
explanation: The conclusion covers every kind of screen, so finding that tablet readers understood as well as paper readers directly undercuts it. Slower reading on phones fits the conclusion, and students' reading habits or the type of article do not show that some screens are fine.

stem:
A forester tracked the share of a forest in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa covered by tree canopy. She notes that the long decline in canopy cover ended in the last period shown: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the text?
options: it fell from 62 percent in 2000 to 55 percent in 2010, which was a drop of 7 percentage points.
it rose from 51 percent in 2010 to 55 percent in 2015, and then rose again to 62 percent in 2020.
after falling from 62 percent in 2000 to 51 percent in 2015, it rose to 53 percent in 2020.
it fell in every period shown, finally reaching its lowest level of 51 percent in the year 2020.
explanation: Cover fell from 62 to 51 percent by 2015 and then rose to 53 in 2020, so the decline ended in the last period. The 2000–2010 drop is accurate but says nothing about the end of the decline, and the other two choices misread the order of the figures.

stem:
A sports scientist claims that skilled cricket batters judge where a delivery will land mainly from the bowler's arm and body movements, before the ball has even left the bowler's hand.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the sports scientist's claim?
options: Skilled batters keep their eyes fixed on the ball for most of its flight from the bowler's hand toward the bat.
Fast bowlers in international cricket can deliver the ball at speeds of more than 140 kilometres per hour.
Shown videos that stopped at the moment of release, skilled batters still predicted where the ball would land far better than chance.
Beginners were less accurate than skilled batters at hitting balls delivered to them by a bowling machine.
explanation: If batters predict accurately from footage that ends at release, they must be reading the bowler's movements before the ball is let go, as the claim says. Watching the ball in flight suggests the opposite, bowling speed is irrelevant, and a machine shows no arm action to read.

stem:
A gardener in Rawalpindi claims that her roses produce more flowers when they are planted in the sunny part of her garden.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the gardener's claim?
options: Her roses are watered every evening, and she feeds them with compost twice a year.
Roses in the shady bed kept their leaves later into the autumn than the roses in the sunny bed did.
Her neighbour grows roses of a different variety along a wall that faces north.
Roses of the same variety produced twice as many flowers in the sunny bed as in the shady bed.
explanation: Comparing the same variety in sunny and shady beds tests the claim directly, and the sunny bed flowered more. Watering, autumn leaves and a neighbour's roses do not compare flowering in sun and shade.

stem:
A motoring reviewer compared three car models. She notes that the car that travels farthest on a full tank is not the most fuel-efficient of the three. ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the reviewer's point?
options: Model Z travels only 540 km on a full tank, which is the shortest distance of any of the three models tested.
Model X travels 600 km on its 40-litre tank, which works out at a fuel efficiency of 15 km per litre.
Model Y goes 650 km on a full tank, and at 18 km per litre it is also the most efficient of the three models.
Model Y goes 650 km on a full tank, but at 13 km per litre it is less efficient than Model Z, at 18 km per litre.
explanation: Y goes farthest but manages 650 ÷ 50 = 13 km per litre, while Z manages 540 ÷ 30 = 18, so the farthest-travelling car is not the most efficient. Z's short range and X's 15 km per litre are accurate but do not make the comparison, and Y's efficiency is 13, not 18.
